profiles.summary: The state that Arbitrum One settles on Ethereum is computed by a WebAssembly build of the replay binary made with go1.25.9, while the public endpoint is a native go1.27.3 build of an unpublished release. The 31 assertions confirmed on Ethereum in the last 9,000 blocks commit to the same block hashes as the public node for L2 blocks 524,847,627 to 525,199,572, and all reruns match the specification.

deltas.delta: The canonical state transition is the replay binary cmd/replay built with GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm (Makefile lines 477-480) by a pinned go1.25.9 (Dockerfile line 73), shipped as WAVM machine consensus-v61 with root 0xc10cd7ec6acaf1c441a3f6bd0900ad20f15855ba775a96f1939118cbc629dc97 (Dockerfile line 206). The consensus-v61 tag pins go1.25.9 and holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 as well. Validators therefore run core/vm and uint256 through the Go WebAssembly backend, where math/bits multiplication, division and carries are not the arm64 or amd64 intrinsics the public node uses.

eth_call wasmModuleRoot() on the Arbitrum One rollup 0x4DCeB440657f21083db8aDd07665f8ddBe1DCfc0 returns 0xc10cd7ec...dc97 (the consensus-v61 root). The 31 AssertionConfirmed events between Ethereum blocks 26,476,173 and 26,485,045 carry block hashes and send roots that equal eth_getBlockByHash on the public node for L2 blocks 524,847,627 to 525,199,572, a range holding at least 27,391 PoolManager logs. So for that range the WebAssembly path and the native go1.27.3 path agree on every state root (research/network-risk/cycles/011/arbitrum-family.work/raw/arb1_assertion_vs_node.json).
deltas.source: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call and eth_getLogs, queried 2026-11-24; https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc eth_getBlockByHash

deltas.delta: web3_clientVersion still reports nitro/v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f on linux-arm64 and linux-amd64 with go1.27.3. No v3.13.0 or rc tag is public: raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for go.mod at v3.13.0 and v3.13.0-rc.9, and the CHANGELOG on master is byte identical to the copy taken in cycle 9 (it stops at v3.11.0-rc.6).

holiman/uint256 has no release after v1.3.2 (proxy.golang.org list), and go-ethereum master and v1.17.4 to v1.17.6 pin v1.3.2. The unreleased master of the library rewrites Div and Mod (udiv, umod, one Knuth step per divisor size) and adds a shift path for divisors that are powers of two, the shape of FullMath.sol:62, 67 and 73. A transcription of the new code gave no mismatch against Python integers on 298,076 random and edge cases and 21,792 cases shaped like FullMath and TickMath.sol:104 (research/network-risk/cycles/011/arbitrum-family.work/scripts/uint256_master_div.py, raw/uint256_master_div.json, raw/uint256_master_twos.json). No network runs it today.

Reruns on 2026-11-24 with client versions logged before each script (research/network-risk/cycles/011/arbitrum-family.work/raw/clientVersions.log): battery.py 99,985 of 99,985 and targeted.py 85,544 of 85,544 as specified on all three; pmdiff.py 250 of 250 identical on all three; pmdiff2.py 300 of 300 on Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain and 299 of 300 on Elysium, the exception being script 189 again, the out of gas case already cleared in cycle 9; swaps.py found no tick mismatch.

findings.title: Arbitrum family validators compute the settled state with a go1.25.9 WebAssembly build that public endpoints do not run
findings.difference: On Ethereum the client that answers eth_call also produces the state. On these three chains the state that the parent chain accepts, and so the state behind every withdrawal, is defined by the replay binary compiled by go1.25.9 to WebAssembly (GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm) and published as WAVM machine consensus-v61. The public endpoints and, as far as anyone can see, the sequencers run a native arm64 or amd64 build of nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 made with go1.27.3. The two paths compile the same go-ethereum fork and holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 with different Go releases and different code generators.
findings.mechanism: Every opcode test in this review, including the 185,529 vectors, the 550 scripts and the reruns of this cycle, ran on the native build. If the WebAssembly build of uint256 or core/vm computed one MULMOD in FullMath.sol:24 or 48, one SDIV in TickBitmap, or one JUMPI differently, a swap would produce one state on the sequencer and another in the replay. The sequencer's state is what users see and what the next transactions build on; the replay's state is what an honest validator asserts on the parent chain. An ordinary account cannot cause such a split unless a codegen difference exists, and none is known. The comparison of confirmed assertions with node block hashes over 31 assertions on Arbitrum One, 57 on Robinhood Chain and 6 on Elysium found no split, which covers every PoolManager transaction in those ranges.
findings.impact: No loss path. A split would stall confirmations and withdrawals to the parent chain for all users until the operators reconciled the two paths, and pool funds would stay where they are.
findings.preconditions: A difference between the go1.25.9 WebAssembly build and the go1.27.3 native build on an instruction the PoolManager uses. None is known.
findings.mitigations: Deployers can watch confirmed assertions against their own node, as done here. Operators can build the native node with the Go release of the consensus machine.

sources.supports: replay.wasm is built with GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm (lines 477-480)
go1.25.9 is pinned for the wasm build (line 73) and consensus-v61 root 0xc10cd7ec... is downloaded (line 206)
public endpoint is nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 built with go1.27.3

cleared.check: Does the state that Arbitrum One confirms on Ethereum, computed by the consensus-v61 WebAssembly replay, equal the state of the native go1.27.3 public node over a recent range with PoolManager activity?
cleared.result: Yes. All 31 AssertionConfirmed events in Ethereum blocks 26,476,173 to 26,485,045 name block hashes and send roots that the node returns for L2 blocks 524,847,627 to 525,199,572, which hold at least 27,391 PoolManager logs. A block hash commits to the state root, so both paths computed the same balances, storage and pool state.
cleared.source: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_getLogs on 0x4DCeB440657f21083db8aDd07665f8ddBe1DCfc0 and https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc eth_getBlockByHash, 2026-11-24; research/network-risk/cycles/011/arbitrum-family.work/raw/arb1_assertion_vs_node.json

cleared.check: The same comparison for Robinhood Chain.
cleared.result: 57 of 57 confirmed nodes in Ethereum blocks 26,476,112 to 26,485,027 match the public node for L2 blocks 116,044,749 to 117,068,132.

cleared.check: Do Elysium's block hashes equal the assertions confirmed on HyperEVM for a recent window?
cleared.result: Yes for the window checked: six assertions confirmed on HyperEVM under the consensus-v61 root equal the Elysium node's block hashes for L2 blocks 9,796,929 to 9,884,174. This is the operator's validator agreeing with the operator's node. The rollup has one whitelisted validator, the EOA 0x8e87f7c65750c25c6708de33823124cf457676b2, which sent the confirming transactions itself, and the whitelist is enabled. It is not an independent replay, so the unnamed vlocal+unknown go1.25.12 build rests on the opcode battery and the PoolManager scripts run against the endpoint. Robinhood Chain is in the same position with two whitelisted validators.

cleared.check: Is the consensus path exposed to Go issue 81863, the dead store miscompile of go1.26.0 to go1.26.10 and go1.27.0 to go1.27.3?
cleared.result: No. The WAVM machine that defines the settled state is built with go1.25.9 at both v3.12.4 and the consensus-v61 tag, and the bad compiler commit landed after the go1.25 branch, as cycle 9 recorded. Only the native nodes carry it, which F-117 already covers.

cleared.check: Has holiman/uint256 or upstream go-ethereum moved to new arithmetic code that these chains might pick up with v3.13.0?
cleared.result: There is no release after v1.3.2, and go-ethereum master and v1.17.4 to v1.17.6 still pin v1.3.2. The unreleased master of uint256 rewrites Div and Mod and adds a shift path for power-of-two divisors (the FullMath.sol:62, 67, 73 shape). A transcription of that code matched Python integers on 298,076 general cases and 21,792 FullMath and TickMath.sol:104 shaped cases. It needs a fresh test whenever a release pins it. Two planted faults were caught: one wrong bit in the two-limb quotient gave 2,517 mismatches in 19,873 cases, and an off-by-one shift in the power-of-two path gave 148 (raw/uint256_master_planted.txt).

cleared.check: Reruns of battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py and replay.py on this unit's endpoints on 2026-11-24.
cleared.result: All vectors as specified; all scripts identical except Elysium pmdiff2 script 189, the gas case already cleared; 15,038 mined swaps pass the tick relation; 25 of 25 sampled Robinhood multi-step swaps replay to the unit. Arbitrum One no longer serves the old state that 19 of its multi-step samples need.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses: is there a Nitro, ArbOS or Stylus advisory newer than the Stylus activation pause of 2026-10-02 and the ArbOS 60 and 61 review?
cleared.result: None found. The public Nitro tree has no tag after v3.12.4, its changelog is unchanged since cycle 9, and a web search found no newer advisory. The Stylus pause and its liveness bugs are already recorded, at the pool-creator level.

leadResults.answer: v3.13.0 is not tagged. raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for go.mod at v3.13.0 and v3.13.0-rc.9, and the master CHANGELOG is unchanged since cycle 9, so the fork commit it pins cannot be read. Elysium's trace methods still need an API key. Instead, Elysium's block hashes for L2 blocks 9,796,929 to 9,884,174 equal six assertions confirmed on HyperEVM under the consensus-v61 root. For those blocks the node agrees with assertions that the operator's own single whitelisted validator confirmed, which is not an independent replay. The same check on Arbitrum One (31 assertions) and Robinhood Chain (57) ties the unpublished rc.9 to consensus-v61 results as well.

debug_traceCall and debug_traceTransaction on the Elysium endpoint still require an authenticated API key, and no explorer listing failed internal calls was found. The assertion match on Elysium comes from the operator's own validator and is not independent. It is not a direct observation of a reverted unlock frame.

Operator level. Sequencer builds are not published, and the public endpoints still report go1.27.3. The state that settles on the parent chain is computed by the consensus-v61 WebAssembly machine built with go1.25.9, which predates the fault. A sequencer miscompile would therefore show as a split from confirmed assertions, and none appears in the windows checked.
Operator level. No Go toolchain is available, so no SSA dump was made. The consensus path is built with go1.25.9 and does not carry the fault.
